description: Rigid aluminum-honeycomb primary structure with multi-layer thermal insulation (MLI). Standard platform for Earth-orbiting and lunar missions.
tech_notes: Structural dry mass baseline. Houses avionics, thermal louvers, and reaction wheels.
nasa_heritage: Derived from NASA Small Explorer (SMEX) and Landsat structural buses.

description: Reinforced titanium-composite structure with heavy radiation shielding designed to withstand intense interplanetary space environments.
tech_notes: Required for long-duration interplanetary cruise to Mars or outer planetary trajectories.
nasa_heritage: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and Cassini-Huygens structural architecture.

description: 6-wheel drive rocker-bogie differential suspension chassis capable of traversing 40cm Martian boulders and steep inclines.
tech_notes: Enables surface traverse and autonomous navigation. Essential for Mars Rover surface science.
nasa_heritage: Curiosity and Perseverance Mars rover mobility platforms.

description: Surface-affixed triple-junction solar cells. No deployment mechanism needed, providing high reliability at lower power output.
tech_notes: Power output diminishes during orbital eclipse and is reduced by 50% at Mars distance due to the inverse-square law.
nasa_heritage: Pioneer and Lunar Prospector solar arrays.

description: Large articulating flexible solar wings that track the Sun continuously to provide maximum electrical power in orbit.
tech_notes: Provides high peak wattage. Requires deployment verification during initial orbit insertion.
nasa_heritage: NASA Orion, InSight, and Cygnus UltraFlex solar wing technology.

description: Plutonium-238 dioxide radioisotope thermoelectric generator providing continuous, decay-based power unaffected by dust storms, night cycles, or solar distance.
tech_notes: Ideal for Mars surface night operations and deep-space missions where solar irradiance is weak or obscured.
nasa_heritage: Power source for NASA's Curiosity rover, Perseverance rover, and New Horizons.

description: Secondary rechargeable lithium-ion battery package that stores reserve power for planetary eclipse phases and high-demand operations.
tech_notes: Vital buffer preventing brownouts during orbital night or during high-power sensor activation.
nasa_heritage: Standard NASA Goddard Space Flight Center energy storage modules.

description: Visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared pushbroom radiometer capable of mapping global vegetation, water reserves, and coastal changes.
tech_notes: Primary instrument for Earth observation. Requires high data downlink bandwidth to transmit images.
nasa_heritage: Landsat 8 and 9 primary imaging payload (NASA/USGS).

description: Active radar instrument providing high-resolution ground surface deformation mapping through clouds, storms, and darkness.
tech_notes: Significant power consumer, but yields critical geodetic and surface motion scientific datasets.
nasa_heritage: NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR) and Magellan Venus radar mapper.

display_name: Lunar Surface Geophone & Heat Flow Probe
description: Broadband seismic sensor suite measuring deep moonquakes, meteorite impacts, and internal planetary thermal gradients.
tech_notes: Must be deployed securely onto the lunar regolith after touchdown.
nasa_heritage: Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment and Artemis Farside Seismic Suite.

description: 1-meter rotary-percussive drill system equipped with mass spectrometers to extract and analyze sub-surface lunar water ice volatiles.
tech_notes: Critical for proving in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) feasibility on the Moon.
nasa_heritage: VIPER TRIDENT drill system (NASA Ames/Honeybee Robotics).

description: Elevated dual-camera system with 3:1 zoom capability, taking 3D color stereo panoramas and assessing Martian mineralogy from afar.
tech_notes: Required primary reconnaissance instrument for Mars rover operations.
nasa_heritage: Perseverance Mastcam-Z instrument suite.

description: Robotic turret arm carrying a hollow coring drill, dust removal gas tool, and laser-induced breakdown spectrometer (LIBS) for geochemical interrogation.
tech_notes: Collects pristine core samples sealed in hermetic tubes for potential sample return.
nasa_heritage: SuperCam and Sample Caching System on Perseverance Mars rover.

description: Broad-beam omnidirectional antenna providing robust low-bitrate emergency command links regardless of spacecraft pointing attitude.
tech_notes: Reliable for low Earth orbit, but insufficient alone for deep space high-bandwidth science telemetry.
nasa_heritage: Ubiquitous NASA safe-mode communications architecture.

description: Directional horn antenna offering moderate telemetry throughput for lunar and cis-lunar exploration orbits.
tech_notes: Well suited for lunar missions. Requires spacecraft pointing towards Earth.
nasa_heritage: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) telemetry systems.

description: Gimbaled high-frequency Ka/X-band reflector dish capable of establishing high-throughput data pipes across hundreds of millions of kilometers.
tech_notes: Essential for transmitting rich imagery and spectrometer data streams from Mars back to Earth Deep Space Network.
nasa_heritage: Deep Space 1 and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter 3-meter Ka-band system.

description: Catalytic hydrazine thruster clusters for 3-axis attitude control, momentum desaturation, and orbital stationkeeping maneuvers.
tech_notes: Provides reliable short impulses. Sufficient for LEO orbital maintenance.
nasa_heritage: Standard NASA Goddard modular RCS systems.

description: High-thrust chemical rocket engine combining MMH fuel and NTO oxidizer for major trans-lunar and trans-Mars injection burns.
tech_notes: High specific impulse (Isp ~320s). Delivers required delta-v for capture into planetary orbit.
nasa_heritage: Aerojet Rocketdyne R-4D engine used on Apollo CSM, Cassini, and Orion.

description: Electrostatic xenon ion engine producing exceptional fuel efficiency (Isp > 4100s) through continuous low-thrust propulsion.
tech_notes: Exceptional efficiency for deep space cruise. Requires high electrical power input from solar or nuclear systems.
nasa_heritage: NASA NEXT-C thruster flown on the DART planetary defense mission and Dawn probe.

display_name: Throttleable Descent Engines & Lunar Landing Gear
description: Four crushable aluminum honeycomb landing legs with terrain hazard detection LiDAR and throttleable braking thrusters for soft lunar touchdown.
tech_notes: Mandatory system for Lunar Exploration Landers. Absorbs touchdown shocks on regolith.
nasa_heritage: Surveyor, Apollo Lunar Module, and NASA CLPS commercial lander designs.

display_name: Mars Aeroshell, Heat Shield & Supersonic Parachute
description: PICA ablative heat shield enclosure, backshell, and 21.5m disk-gap-band supersonic parachute for surviving Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) in Mars atmosphere.
tech_notes: Dissipates 99% of atmospheric kinetic energy during Mars entry at 20,000 km/h.
nasa_heritage: NASA Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, and Mars 2020 EDL heritage.

display_name: Rocket-Powered Sky Crane Terminal Descent Stage
description: Hovering rocket backpack with nylon bridle tethers that lowers the rover gently directly onto its wheels on the Martian surface before flyaway.
tech_notes: Required for heavy Mars rover soft touchdown without landing legs or ramps.
nasa_heritage: NASA JPL's revolutionary Sky Crane system used on Curiosity and Perseverance.

description: Radiation-hardened central processor with triple modular redundancy (TMR) executing autonomous fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR).
tech_notes: Resistant to solar particle events and Galactic Cosmic Rays. Essential computing core.
nasa_heritage: BAE Systems RAD750 processor flown on Kepler, MRO, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter, and Perseverance.

description: Radiation-tolerant Flash memory buffer with Reed-Solomon error correction to store raw scientific observations prior to scheduled ground passes.
tech_notes: Prevents data loss when high-data instruments observe targets out of line-of-sight with Earth.
nasa_heritage: Standard NASA GSFC solid state recorders for EOS and Planetary missions.
